proposals.evidence: DEDR5548 explicitly gives Gondi Koya vēre separately and vēreton another. The primary does not identify these particular survey lects or prove absence of Telugu contact, so transmission remains a stated limitation of this pending comparison. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

The article also records other Gondi mēlo bad/taboo, so the proposal is confined to these explicitly good responses and does not erase dialectal semantic differences. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR1499 explicitly gives Kannada gāḷi/gāḷ wind, Kodagu gāḷi, Telugu gāli, Gondi (Ko.) gāl and neighbouring gāli forms. The survey gāḷ-/gāl-/gāy- responses retain this wind stem, with the Alu Kurumba lateral-to-glide correspondence and ordinary final vowels preserved; compounds or modified phrases are excluded. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
